newsitem.title: MEXICO: Ahmsa '96 net exceeds high hopes - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Ahmsa '96 net exceeds high hopes - analysts.

text.p: The 1996 results of Mexican steelmaker Altos Hornos de Mexico SA (Ahmsa) were surprising because they came out even more favorable than expected, analysts said.
The company announced Tuesday that earnings per share in 1996 were 9.44 pesos, compared with 1.66 pesos in 1995. A Reuters survey of three analysts forecast an average of 8.56 pesos per share.
Ahmsa's net totalled 3.666 billion pesos against the 645.9 million peso profit the previous year.
Revenues moved up to 11.084 billion pesos versus 9.936 billion pesos the year before.
"It was a great report, basically one of the strongest earnings surprises of the year so far," Abaco analyst Bond Snodgrass said.
He said the company's earnings per share registered about 20 percent above consensus analyst estimates.

Monetary gains did help the company's yearly results, Bondgrass said, but added the company's operating margins took a lighter blow than expected as the company improved operations in the face of higher energy costs.

The company also expects a smaller bite from natural gas expenses in the first quarter of 1997, as domestic prices relaxed from winter highs, he said. The company's new coal injection oven is expected to come on line in coming weeks.

Bondgrass and Solomon Brothers analyst Mauricio Reveco agreed that Ahmsa has been trading at very attractive levels. The stock's nominal shares gained 1.32 pesos Tuesday to close at 17.8 pesos each, while Ahmsa ADR's gained 7/8 to close at 11-1/2. "I think the stock is fairly inexpensive right now. In terms of 12 members of a Latin American peer group, Ahmsa appears the cheapest," Reveco said.
Ahmsa has been aggressive in new projects and has improved shipments, he added. The stock could also be a means of participating in Mexico's expected continuing economic recovery, Reveco said.
"We believe 1997 is certainly the year to take advantage of the steel market," he said.
Ahmsa said on Tuesday it plans $222 million in 1997 investments, to improve processes and overall efficiency.
Projects for the year include improvements in galvanized sheet steel painting, the overhaul in one of its coking plants and establishment of the new coal injection plant.
